key_insight: Legendre-based modified extreme learning machines solve linear convection–diffusion problems without iterative training, outperforming tested PINNs in accuracy and solution time for steady-state and discrete-time formulations.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers an efficient option for transport simulations with steep gradients and sharp boundary layers in convection-dominated regimes.
method: Represent solutions using shifted Legendre polynomial bases.
Determine output weights through a single least-squares solve using the linear governing equations.
Reuse the coefficient-matrix LU or QR factorization across discrete time steps.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covers steady and unsteady high-Peclet benchmarks with continuous and discontinuous boundary conditions, using FEM references and comparisons against PINNs with advanced training strategies.
watch_item: Global continuous-time MELM becomes computationally demanding as the space–time basis grows; PINNs showed better scalability for large space–time formulations.
paper_title: A Legendre-Based Modified Extreme Learning Machine for Convection-Diffusion Equations: Steady-State, Continuous-Time, and Discrete-Time Formulations
